items.title: Dan Wall and Adam Nussbaum interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 19, 2001
items.q: You know people like Art Pepper and all these guys that wrote these books, they were always dealing with that paranoia

ctx.x: What about the racial scene these days? Is it, I mean this music has brought a lot of people together where they weren’t allowed in other parts of society. Is it healthy now for you guys anyway?

You know I’ve never really thought about this stuff in regard to what I do. I just do what I do. I can only try to be the best that I can be. I’m going to be — sorry about that — I know I’m going to be involved in situations and I can only try to play the best I can. I know I won’t get hired by certain white musicians. I know I won’t get hired by certain black musicians. But you know what? Then I know I get hired by certain white musicians and I know I get hired by black musicians. And I’ve found that it’s a…

with Yugoslavia and Serbia and this and Croatia and all the Middle Eastern crap. You know I just look at the common — what do we all have in common. Not what do we all have in difference. I don’t know, what would you say about all that?
